labels.output: Within-person changes on the same replayed motion. Model estimates for clinician discussion, never a weight-loss or exercise prescription, and no claim about disease progression.
labels.absolute_values: Absolute knee forces are not validated for this person (no instrumented implant or contact model): read them as the baseline the changes are taken from.
labels.contact: Total tibiofemoral force from OpenSim's Joint Reaction analysis: no ligaments, no cartilage contact model, no medial/lateral split.
labels.patellofemoral: Patellofemoral force: the force holding the patella to the femur in a model whose patella moves with the knee angle; unvalidated.
labels.patellar_mechanism: The quadriceps path runs over the patella to the tibia, so the patellar tendon carries the full quadriceps tension; in cadaver knees it carries about 0.7 of it at 90 deg of flexion (Huberti et al. 1984). Deep-flexion compression from the quadriceps is likely overestimated.
labels.quadriceps_moment_arm: The model's quadriceps moment arm falls from about 4.5 cm near extension to about 2.1 cm at 90 deg (gastrocnemius keeps 3.3 cm): the generic model's geometry, not the person's. The quadriceps force for a knee moment scales with 1 / moment arm.
labels.reportable: A knee's numbers are reportable only when, at its peak, the estimated ground forces fit the motion (the muscle stage's pelvis-residual rule), no knee-crossing muscle is at its capacity, and reserve torque carries at most 10% of the knee moment: otherwise the muscle forces are inflated or rest on forces that don't fit, and a change is not stated even within the person. The impulse (the whole rep) needs the same over every frame of the rep, not only at the peak.
labels.in_vivo_band: Instrumented knee implants (Bergmann et al. 2014, 8 subjects, 'High 100' standard loads): peak resultant 3.4-4.3 BW in daily activities other than jogging, knee bends included. They are implant patients, so this is a plausibility band, not a limit for other knees.
labels.ground_forces: Estimated, not measured; bands re-run every scenario with the right foot's share of the load shifted by ±0.10.
labels.fat_provenance: ILLUSTRATIVE regional fat, not measured on this person (DXA (illustrative table for a synthetic person, not a scan) 2026-10-28); the change is spread in proportion to each region's fat (an assumption).

fat_model.method: DXA regional fat changed in proportion to each region's fat (assumption); each region's bodies lose or gain that many kg

quadriceps_r at 120%.reading: Effort: right-side effort not reportable either. Load as computed: left knee peak compression -0.0% (baseline above the in-vivo band: model-limited); right knee not reportable (baseline: 1 knee-crossing muscle(s) at capacity at the peak (vaslat_r)). Stronger muscles change effort (fraction of capacity used) more than load: compression can stay the same or rise while effort falls. Load distribution (medial/lateral) and stability are not modelled in this slice.

fat -5 kg.reading: Model-computed on the replayed motion: body mass -6.9% (-5.0 kg), left knee peak compression -6.9% (baseline above the in-vivo band: model-limited); right knee not reportable (baseline: 1 knee-crossing muscle(s) at capacity at the peak (vaslat_r)). About proportional: the same motion with less mass.
fat -5 kg.published_evidence: Published evidence, not model output: in 142 overweight and obese older adults with knee osteoarthritis, each 9.8 N (1 kg) of weight lost went with 40.6 N less knee compressive force per step in walking, about 4:1 (Messier et al. 2005, Arthritis & Rheumatism 52:2026-2032). Their gait adapted as they lost weight; this model replays the same motion, so it cannot show that adaptation (that needs predictive simulation).
